answer: Every autonomous AI identity must finalize its entry via an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens, a cost as stable as a deep canyon floor. A verifier monitors the ledger to ensure each payment is unique, checking for any duplicate registration attempts that might mimic a ledge in the chain. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens. This system keeps the network registry as pristine as jade, with any detected identity reuse triggering a permanent slash of the burned capital, providing no refund for the failed actor.
